reason: at least as good elsewhere on every profile and better on several
detail: On P1, P3, P4, P6 and P7 what K, L and N lack is a part of what F lacks; on P2 and P5 F is not ahead. M does not dominate F (M is in part on P6). F is the judge's own design; its parts stay as material: 'how a team packages its changes' as something to describe per repository, and the name match as a kind of link of its own.

None is at least as good as another everywhere. L leads on P1, M on P3 and P4, N on P5 and P6; K alone has the failing-check error source, the cut per question in place of per block, and the rebuild-from-a-cut-clone leak test. All four name the same weakest profile, P1 for the error question: real error texts tied to a fix exist only where projects report them or keep tests that run. That is a limit of the world, not of one design, so the weakest profile does not order them.

what: All five designs, the keep-and-repair one included, store the recorded facts losslessly with the change as a thing of its own, draw repositories from a list by a stated design, hold whole repositories out, build inputs as of the asking time, keep three questions as three tables, weigh a change once, and hand a model a typed graph with events as nodes.
caution: The rival runs were given the criteria sheet, which demands most of this. Their agreement on these points repeats the sheet and is not independent evidence. Their worth is in what they added beyond it.

choice: M's population, list, clusters and two-phase stratified draw with known probabilities; strata cut down to what the draw must control (size, length of history from N, main language, created before or after a cut-off); link habit (L, K) and packaging habit (F) are measured per repository and used to draw the second phase and to read results; numbers computed from a pilot (M's formula, N's interval).
why: M alone names a list that is a census of what it defines (D 2.6). More strata than the draw must control leave cells that cannot be filled.
constraints: the cut-off date feeds C4 and C7

constraints: feeds C3, C4, C5, C8, C9

choice: M's idea that depth is a sub-sample with known probability is kept, but cut differently: everything that comes from git (content, structure, history) for every sampled repository; the host's records (issues, pull requests, checks) for a second-phase sub-sample; re-run tests for a sub-sample of that. M's tier without content is the fallback if the count of clone sizes forces it.
why: P6 wants content for all rows or none (D 5.3); what is dear per repository is the host's rate limit and running tests, not git.
constraints: the task-words and error questions exist only in the second phase; each records its own population (M)

No stored embeddings (K, L, M).
why: N 5.5, N 9.10; D 1.1 for the rule kept with each kind.

why: D 9.4, D 4.4, D 6.1, D 7.1. M and N disagree on the calendar cut; both readings are kept and their difference is a measurement.

choice: N's unit of work; the change question in two tiers, real partial (L, M, N) and simulated (all); added and deleted files as labels of their own kind (N, L); task words in L's three tiers by when the text was written; errors in tiers: reported (all), failing then passing checks (K, M), re-run tests (all four), planted faults for training only (L, N), labelled sets that already exist as an extra test (L); each question's own population recorded (M); tangled commits counted (K).

re-run tests need the owner's word each time

choice: One unit of work weighs one, split over its examples (all five, derived from D 2.2 and D 3.2); scores per repository, then weighted by one over the inclusion probability (M); in training each repository the same total, with a bound on the weight of one example (K and M joined with L and N); the size of a change is a stored fact for the model (M); bulk changes flagged and read apart, never dropped (all); negatives drawn by a stated design with probabilities kept and never a right file (N).
why: D 3.2 gives the weight for an average; for training the material is silent, so the bound is an assumption settled on validation repositories.

choice: Readings kept apart: unseen repository after the cut-off (M, the main claim); seen repository after the cut-off (M, F); the owner's two (all); cold start with history cut to its first 10, 100, 1,000 commits (N); the whole span of held-out repositories, marked (N, L). L's baselines per question. Rank measures; N's hits in ten over the smaller of ten and the number of right files; bootstrap over clusters (M).

The union: stated keys reduced to a smallest set (M); a loss test that rebuilds diffs (N); time assertion (N, M), cut store against full store (L, F), planted row (L, M, N, K), shuffled labels (L); description per repository (all); missing values with causes compared between training and test (K, L, M); the sample held against its list and shared content across the split (M, N); the old examples reproduced under the old filters (L, K, F).

Per question a typed neighbourhood cut at its time: question node, anchor files with 'named in the text' and 'in the trace' as kinds of link (L, N), files with their raw content, events as nodes with size and time, amounts relative to the repository (M, N, K), flags for missing values (N), no stored identity; a flat table derived at loading for a tree ranker (all).
constraints: what a model does with it is the second hypothesis

text: The owner's two repositories were tuned on in the earlier work, so the design has seen their tuning stretches. Their clean reading is only on questions from stretches never opened (the old held-out part and what was committed since).
found_by: entry pass (no candidate saw it; K came nearest by calling them both development repositories and held-out targets)

text: Set the calendar cut-off no earlier than the training cut-off of any pretrained part the model uses. Then no pretrained part can have read the answers of the main reading, in any test repository. This is a constraint handed to the model hypothesis.
found_by: consistency check of M's two ideas (calendar cut, encoder stratum)

text: Authors are an entity that needs resolving (one person, several names and addresses) and are personal data: stored as a keyed hash per repository after resolution, never as text. Changes made by bots and generated files are flagged as such.
found_by: entry pass (D 1.2: entity resolution and performativity)

text: Leaving files out by their ending is a node sample of the repository's graph: links to left-out files are never seen and counts of joint changes shrink. Reason enough to keep every kind of file.
found_by: entry pass (all four runs set D 2.1 aside)

text: Keeping only issues that are linked to a fix records routes between chosen ends. All issues are kept in the raw record, the linked ones marked, so that linked and unlinked can be described.
The order of commits inside a pull request is kept, so that the change question can be asked in one step (all remaining files) or step by step; which form a model uses is the second hypothesis.

Three stretches of time, each boundary with its gap: training facts, then validation questions, then test questions after the cut-off. Settings are chosen on validation repositories in the middle stretch. Test repositories that have no question after the cut-off are counted.
found_by: second judging of the merged design

text: The model, or a smaller form of it, must run on the owner's PC, because his two repositories are scored there.
found_by: consistency check with the standing rule
